stalls_and_misroutes.lead_arm_stalls: T2 and T3 in sets 2 and 6: the lead named the likely holder to alice but addressed only alice, so no agent that held the facts woke, and no correct message came. The pre-registered run has no follow-up from alice, which is what a person would normally send next.
stalls_and_misroutes.lead_arm_misroutes: No address to a holder: T2 and T3 in sets 2 and 6. T4 in sets 2, 4 and 6 had no address to release, though the lead had no way to know of the blocker. No lead addressed an agent that held nothing relevant.
stalls_and_misroutes.today_arm_stalls: None for an answer. In set 5, release didn't surface the T4 blocker.

findings: Cost: excluding launch, the lead arm used 25 to 43 model calls per set against 66 to 67 today, and 1.08M to 1.88M cache-read tokens against 3.11M to 3.18M: on average 48% of the calls and 43% of the cache-read tokens.

Task success: today's arm answered T1, T2 and T3 in all 3 sets. The lead arm answered T1 in 3 of 3, and T2 and T3 in 1 of 3 each. The saving includes work that didn't get done, so the cost figures aren't a like-for-like saving.
Unprompted help: release raised the T4 blocker in 2 of 3 sets today and 0 of 3 with a lead. This is the loss the proposal predicted.

Routing: in the one set where the lead addressed the holders (set 4), the T3 finished in 18 seconds against 6.5 to 11 today, with 9 message wakes and 17 calls against 9 to 15 and 15 to 20 today. In the other two sets the lead addressed only alice and named the likely holder in its text, despite the event text 'answer an unaddressed message, or address whoever should act'.
Today's arm repeats itself: agents with nothing to add sent 'not in my notes' messages, and those messages woke the others again (9 message wakes for a one-answer task).
Roster wakes aren't affected by the rule: each conversation start cost 3 roster wakes in both arms, so the lead arm's per-task costs include them.
not_shown: A lead with better guidance, a lead that knows other agents' areas, or a person following up. Any of them could change T2 and T3; none was tried, since the run allowed no changes.
Long conversations, larger rosters, cross-machine networks, Codex or OpenCode, sleeping or offline leads, an author who can't reach the lead, a lead leaving, and hosts that haven't upgraded.
Model calls per wake on real projects or user settings: the runs had small fixture projects and no user settings, so token totals don't predict real costs.
A parked window on a long gap: parked rows were gathered in only 3 wakes, in set 4's T2 and T3.

deviations.change: Claude Code ran with --setting-sources project,local and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1, in both arms.
deviations.reason: Not in the pre-registration. Keeps user settings and memory out of the runs, and stops memory carrying between sets. Token totals are lower than for a session with user settings.

deviations.change: Two pilots, not one: a launch with no message, then the pre-registered hello.
deviations.reason: The first stopped after launch to learn the prompts. Neither saw a task. Their usage counts toward the ceiling, and their results aren't used.

deviations.change: run_set.py was committed after the pre-registration and before the first model run.
deviations.reason: It needed the launch prompts, which needed a pilot. The pilot's usage is counted. The tasks, rubric and metrics didn't change.

deviations.change: The lead's tool description text depends on the adapter's environment, and only its presence in the adapter's environment was checked, not the text the model saw. The event text was the checked channel.

deviations.reason: The pre-registration runs it only for ambiguous results, and none was ambiguous on review: every pattern match was a plain statement, and no miss gave the answer another way. The rubric was applied by script, and its author could see the arms.
